cards.subject: Felwood was this forest
lines: During the Third War Tichondrius used the Skull of Gul'dan here, and the corruption spread north.
Felwood is not a separate place. It is Ashenvale, poisoned — the same trees, one border away. Walk north and the ground tells you where it stopped.

cards.subject: Zoram Strand
cards.tag: The cave at the west end
lines: Blackfathom Deeps has a real name: Lathar'Lazal, the Seat of the Sky — a temple to Elune built by Queen Azshara, with gem-encrusted bridges.
The Sundering dropped it into the sea.
What is left is a hole in the rock at the end of a level twenty beach.

cards.subject: Cenarius died in this forest
lines: The Warsong were clear-cutting Ashenvale with goblin help when the demigod came for them. Grom drank Mannoroth's blood and killed him.
Every druid, dryad and keeper you meet here is his child or his student.
The Sentinels, the Cenarion Circle, the Silverwing oath — all of it is grief with a job.

cards.subject: Astranaar
lines: The town sits on an island in a lake with two bridges onto it. That is a defensive shape, not a decorative one.
Raene Wolfrunner runs it as a military post, expecting the Thistlefur furbolgs to eventually come at the town directly.

cards.subject: Xavian · Satyrnaar · Fire Scar
lines: The satyr holds are what is left of the War of the Satyr, more than nine thousand years before the war you are in.
The fel magic that scarred the forest then is the same corruption still eating the Ruins of Stardust.
Ashenvale's demons are not an invasion. They are an infection that never cleared.

cards.subject: The Shrine of Mel'Thandris
lines: Mel'Thandris died sealing away the Druids of the Scythe, and the Scythe of Elune was laid at her shrine here.
Her niece Velinde Starsong came to take it back. The worgen now in the ruins are what renamed the valley.
This is where worgen enter the story. The trail out of it leads to Duskwood.

cards.subject: Dartol's Rod of Transformation
lines: You assemble a broken rod, then use it to turn yourself into a furbolg so you can walk into the Barrow Dens and talk to one.
The disguise is the mechanic and the point: they are corrupted, not hostile by nature.
The chain ends with Ran Bloodtooth's skull, which Raene keeps in a place of reverence.

cards.subject: Ordanus
lines: A keeper of the grove, and the Horde quest on him is a level twenty-nine kill order.
He is not elite. One player takes his head.
The whole questline was deleted in 4.0.3a and he turns up alive again decades later.

cards.subject: Bough Shadow
lines: A Great Tree and one of the portals into the Emerald Dream, guarded in the open world by green dragons and their oracles and boughguards.
No quest sends a levelling player here.
You have to go looking for it.

cards.subject: Silverwing Grove
lines: The Alliance entrance to Warsong Gulch is a physical spot in this zone, southwest of Silverwing Outpost near Fallen Sky Lake.
You can walk to it instead of queueing.
The Horde side is not in Ashenvale at all — it is a mountainside in the Barrens.

cards.subject: Why the Gulch exists
lines: The Warsong Outriders keep logging Ashenvale after the Third War, and the vanilla framing is that they do it despite Thrall.
The Silverwing Sentinels will not rest until every last orc is defeated and cast out.
It is a lumber dispute nobody will end.

cards.subject: The Monument to Grom Hellscream
lines: A stone in the far southeast reads: "Here lies Grommash Hellscream, Chieftain of the Warsong Clan."
At the Harvest Festival, an orc outside Orgrimmar hands Horde players an offering to carry all the way here and lay at its base.
It is the only place in this world where the Horde formally grieves.
